rawOutputSnippet:
## 1. Why a single shared pool fails

A global pool limits total connections, but it does not allocate them fairly.

- Tenant 1’s 100 requests can occupy most or all available pool slots. Other tenants then wait behind Tenant 1’s work in the FIFO queue.
- FIFO ordering preserves arrival order, not tenant fairness. A burst from one tenant can monopolize both active connections and queue capacity.
